title: Katherine Palakovich ("Kittie")

infobox.name: Katherine Palakovich
infobox.role: Director of Business Affairs, Creative License; notary public
infobox.known_for: Sent Dan his own CL non-compete agreement in 2011, then in 2012 notarized the false statements Kevin McKiernan used to try to get Dan's LinkedIn profile terminated

body:
Katherine Palakovich was Director of Business Affairs at
[[wiki/work/creative-license|Creative License]] and, notably, a notary
public — a detail that becomes load-bearing at the end of Dan's time at the
company. She appears on both ends of the relationship's documented arc: in
May 2011 she sent Dan his own non-disclosure/non-compete agreement to sign
("Here is the non-disclosure/non-compete agreement for CL. Please review
and let me know if you have any questions/comments. Thanks, Kittie"), and
she is a routine, friendly presence throughout 2011 in Dan's day-to-day
sick-day and scheduling emails ("Hey Kittie, just wanted to let you know
I'm expecting to be a little bit late this morning").

In June 2012, four months after Dan left the company, [[wiki/people/kevin-mckiernan|Kevin
McKiernan]] filed a formal LinkedIn intellectual-property complaint
against Dan's profile, backed by **two documents Katherine had notarized**
asserting Dan had never been a CL employee and had fabricated his job
title. Dan's email to her, addressed directly and by nickname ("Hi
Kittie"), names the problem precisely: "the notarization of documents
which the notary public believes to be false, deceptive, or fraudulent is
forbidden by the Notary Public Code of Professional Responsibility" — a
specific, cited allegation that she used her own professional credential
to certify a statement she should have known was false, on behalf of her
employer, against a coworker whose employment the company's own accounting
department had spent the preceding two months corresponding with Dan
about in writing.

Despite this, the relationship apparently survived in some form: in
December 2014, by then leaving the company herself
(`kpalakovich@gmail.com`), Katherine bcc'd Dan on a mass "Ex-Creative
License Happy Hour" invitation — "Its my great pleasure to let you guys
know that I QUIT Creative License this week!!!! ... Hope you guys can make
it to have a drink with me" — addressed to "all my favorite ex (and
current) CL employees." Whether Dan attended, or whether the June 2012
notarization was ever discussed between them again, is unrecorded.

**Gaps:** whether Katherine's notarization was made knowingly or under
instruction from McKiernan without independent verification is unresolved
— the corpus has Dan's accusation but not her side. Her life or career
after leaving Creative License in January 2015 is undocumented.
